title: A childhood silver ring in Butte; his nickname 'Buster'
summary: Gil recalls a ring his mother brought him when he was about ten in Montana, remembering her mandolin and his family nicknames.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It's the first ring I've really had for a long time. Because my mother bought me one once when she went to work in (Yellowstone?) National Park when I was living in Butte, Montana. I stayed there with my step-father who was working the mines and my mother took a cooking job in (Gardner?) which is the entrance to Yellowstone National Park. And she brought me back a greatest ring. It was silver and it had a black onyx top with two silver bears standing on their hind legs. (LAUGHTER). I left it in a, I left it in a hotel I think. ( ?).
He told me that she said, Buster don't forget the mandolin. That was his job to remember the mandolin whenever they moved.
And now we've come up with a family nickname too, huh, Buster. What do you call him?
People used to call me that
and my mother didn't know who they were asking for. She remembered that my name was Gil. She named me as Gilmore... different names.
